  "text": "Ada kept the square between two fingers. The ink was wet.

“Wait for what?” Elias whispered.

The constable answered in Ada’s voice. “For me.”

His mouth had not moved. The black line around his finger tightened, and he lifted his hand toward the sealed stone. Three knocks came from inside it. After a pause, three more answered from the yellow door.

Mara helped Venn to his feet. A red groove circled his wrist, though the wall had held him by the other arm. He stared at the mark.

“That’s mine,” the constable said. This time his lips moved.

Dust spilled from the gap at Ada’s knees. She looked through it and saw a strip of lamplight, then the toe of a boot. Its heel was worn unevenly.

She pulled back. Across the cellar, the constable was standing on both feet.

“Elias,” she said, “give me the ledger.”

He passed it over. Ada opened to the page beneath the cellar drawing. A fresh line appeared, letter by letter: DO NOT OPEN FOR THE ONE WHO KNOCKS.

The yellow door shuddered. Mara braced it with her shoulder, and Venn caught the handle.

Ada set the ledger against the gap. The boot on the other side withdrew. Ink-stained fingers reached out, not for the book but for the folded square in her hand.

She gave it back. The fingers pressed the paper flat against the stone. A second word appeared beneath WAIT: UNTIL.

The constable struck the floor with his heel. From beyond the yellow door came the scrape that should have followed."
